title: Fluid type and spacing with clamp()
learningObjectives: Explain fluid type and spacing with clamp() and apply it to responsive components.

understand.concept: clamp(min, preferred, max) calculates a value that grows or shrinks within defined bounds. It is commonly used for responsive typography and spacing. The preferred expression may use viewport or container units, while minimum and maximum values protect usability.
understand.whyItMatters: Unbounded fluid values can become too small or too large. Use sensible limits and test text zoom, narrow screens, and longer translated content.
understand.analogy: clamp() is a flexible measuring tape with a minimum stop and a maximum stop.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; media and container queries use formal CSS conditions and sizing references.

explain.narrative: The page spacing and type scale fluidly but stay between the chosen minimum and maximum values.

practise.guidedTask: Create a responsive heading and spacing system using clamp(). Explain the minimum, preferred, and maximum values.
practise.independentTask: Build a reusable component and test it at different viewport and container sizes, with long labels and text enlargement.
hints: Inspect the actual query condition and container.
Test just below and above thresholds.
Keep content and keyboard order logical.

questions.prompt: Which argument in clamp() expresses the preferred fluid value?
questions.explanation: clamp() uses the middle expression as its preferred value, bounded by the first and third arguments.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable responsive test?
options: Test different widths and content lengths
Test only at one standard phone size
questions.answer: Test different widths and content lengths
questions.explanation: Responsive behaviour depends on actual space and content, not just a device label.
